currentUserGoal: Implement the community suggestion that Grass Touching Simulator should be operable by browser/AI agents instead of exposing only a canvas surface.
changesMade: Added a real DOM agent-control layer for the redesign route while preserving Phaser/canvas as the visual presentation layer.
Created src/game/redesign/RedesignDomBridge.ts to mirror critical redesign state into a readable HTML output and stable HTML buttons.
Exposed document.documentElement.dataset.grassAgentDom = ready while the DOM bridge is mounted.
Added stable DOM controls for roots, Dew Pulse, Root Salve, Soft Touch, Deeper Roots, locked Tiny Sprinkler, locked Scourge Sense, and Begin Next Run.
Refactored root-touch handling so DOM root buttons and canvas root clicks use the same touchRootNode logic.
Connected the DOM bridge to the existing browser debug snapshot so button bounds, disabled state, phase, objective, HP, RT, permanent memory, and meta-screen state stay synchronized.
Added CSS for the agent layer so it is visually unobtrusive during human play but focusable/readable for browser automation and keyboard-style inspection.
Updated the redesign spec and implementation plan to document the DOM agent layer and its browser-smoke expectations.

Browser smoke reached dormancy, confirmed memory/locked/meta DOM controls existed, clicked redesign-begin-next-run-button, and confirmed the next run returned to active.

knownIssues: This is not a full HTML rewrite. The game still uses Phaser/canvas for visuals and most presentation; the DOM layer mirrors the critical controls/state for operability.
The DOM layer currently covers the redesign prototype route only.
Only the existing first-pass run tools and memory nodes are represented; future controls need to be mirrored into the DOM bridge as they are added.
There is still no player-facing options/settings menu.
The old game still exists on the default route and obsolete stress routes; use ?redesign for the new mechanics work.
nextRecommendedSteps: Keep using DOM locators for new browser smoke tests whenever a control has a real gameplay action.
Add options/settings next, with real DOM-accessible controls from the start.
When Tiny Sprinkler becomes functional, add it to the DOM bridge and smoke it through DOM locators.
Consider making the readable state output more structured if external agents need richer summaries than plain text.
doNotRevert: Do not remove the DOM agent layer as dead UI; it is intentional architecture for agent/browser operability.
Do not replace the visual canvas with plain div gameplay unless the user explicitly asks for a visual technology change.
Do not force browser smoke tests back to approximate canvas coordinates when stable DOM controls exist.
Do not use the obsolete ?stress route as evidence of redesign progress.
